Fukushima dumps first batch of once-radioactive water into sea, says it's filtered and safe.
Strictly speaking, water cannot become radioactive. If all the salts, metals and other dissolved goodies that can be radioactive is filtered out, then it's all good.

Technically, you could have tritiated water, which would be radioactive itself. However, the half-life and biological retention is very short.

Essentially though, you are correct. Most of the contamination in the water will come from Cs-137, Co-60, and a few other isotopes typical to this type of reactor. There are numerous ways to remove these contaminants, but most likely a resin filter bead (for ion capture) was used, which means that water is likely cleaner than what comes out of your tap. We normally just evaporate the water here (within tritium release limits), and deal with the remaining salts as we do with other low level wastes.
